summary: xAI announced a new 'workflows' feature in Grok Build that lets the tool plan a task, fan it out across up to 1,024 parallel background agents with verification steps, and return a single consolidated report, with workflows savable as reusable team slash commands.

mechanisms.reason: The product explicitly moves work from a single conversational agent to many autonomous parallel agents executing delegated subtasks in the background.
mechanisms.quote: orchestration scripts that fan a task out across hundreds of parallel agents, verify the results, and report back in one background run

mechanisms.reason: Each workflow run can spawn up to a thousand agents, meaning many more model calls are issued per user task than a single-agent session.
mechanisms.quote: Runs get a budget of 128 agents, and up to 1,024 for big jobs.

practices.reason: The phased, multi-agent script pattern with roll-up and adversarial verification is a concrete orchestration design an engineering team could study for building their own multi-agent pipelines, though it is delivered only through xAI's own tool.
practices.quote: Grok plans the task as a small script: the phases of work, the agents in each phase, and how their results roll up.

practices.reason: The built-in adversarial verification step (independent skeptics checking findings before synthesis) is a transferable measurement idea but described only as an internal feature of xAI's tool.
practices.quote: the plan can build in checks a single pass can't, like independent skeptics verifying every finding before it reaches the final report

practices.reason: Saved workflows become new team-shared slash commands, a minor interface addition for teams already using Grok Build.
practices.quote: workflows in .grok/workflows/ are shared with your team, and ones in ~/.grok/workflows/ follow you everywhere

notable_reason: Concrete disclosure of agentic workload scale (up to 1,024 parallel background agents per task) is a useful data point for tracking growth in agentic inference volume.
